name: AtomStack A20 Pro V2
tagline: Current Atomstack A20 Pro generation: 20W with F60 air assist ecosystem
tldr: AtomStack A20 Pro V2 replaces the older A20 Pro with updated optics and bundle options. Mid-tier Atomstack between P1 and A40: strong detail, not the highest watt class.
mainObjective: Current-gen Atomstack 20W for fine engraving and moderate cutting

priceRange.note: Official Atomstack store, Oct 2026: $369 to $729 depending on bundle

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: 0.08 × 0.10 mm spot and 400 mm/s top speed on Atomstack's spec sheet: good detail on photos and small text
Safety basics included: flame detection (with the Z2 Z-axis slider), tip-over alarm above 15° and resume after interruption
Optional 1.8W 1064 nm IR module ($269 in October 2026) adds bare-metal marking on the same frame
cons: Work area is 400 × 365 mm, shorter than the 400 × 400 mm frames it is often compared with
Cutting past ~5 mm basswood turns multi-pass: compare the A40 Pro V2 if cutting dominates
Manual focus only, and Atomstack does not publish a per-thickness cutting chart for the V2
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W SKU on AtomStack A20 Pro V2. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Use the benchmarks on this profile for quotes. Test on scrap before production.
primaryUse: Mid-range Atomstack diode for detailed work.

editorialDepth.advantages: AtomStack A20 Pro V2 20W is the versatile hobby / side-business SKU: clean engraving and light wood or leather cuts with comparable benchmarks on Maker Atlas.
editorialDepth.limitations: Open-frame: glasses and exhaust required. Not a CO₂ replacement for clear acrylic or heavy thick-stock production.

faq.question: How thick can the A20 Pro V2 cut?
faq.answer: Atomstack's V2 page lists wood and black acrylic among cutting materials but gives no thickness per pass. The earlier A20 Pro was marketed as cutting 12 mm solid wood in one pass, a best-case figure. Our profile lists 5 mm basswood, and our benchmark cuts a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood in ~6–10 min at 4–10 mm/s.

faq.question: What does the A20 Pro V2 cost in October 2026?
faq.answer: On Atomstack's US store: $369 machine-only, $409 basic bundle, $449 air bundle, $489 enclosure or pro bundle, $619 rotary bundle and $729 all-in-one. The spare 20W module was $279. Prices move often with promotions, so check the bundle contents rather than the headline discount.

faq.question: A20 Pro V2 or A40 Pro V2: which one?
faq.answer: The A20 Pro V2 suits engraving-led work and occasional thin cuts. The A40 Pro V2 switches between 24W and 48W, is marketed for much thicker one-pass cuts and was $769 machine-only in October 2026, about $400 more. If you mainly engrave gifts and signs, the 20W is the better use of money.

standoutFeatures.title: Safety sensors included
standoutFeatures.body: Flame detection (requires the Z2 Z-axis slider), tip-over alarm above 15° and resume engraving after a stop, per Atomstack's spec sheet.

standoutFeatures.title: IR add-on for metal
standoutFeatures.body: Atomstack's R20-A 1.8W 1064 nm module fits the A20 Pro V2 and marks bare metal that a blue diode handles poorly ($269 in October 2026).

standoutFeatures.title: Fine 0.08 × 0.10 mm spot
standoutFeatures.body: A tight spot for a 20W diode, which keeps photo dithering and small lettering clean.
